API-REQ-1-1-1-AUTH-CLIENT.content: {"interface_id": "API-REQ-1-1-1-AUTH-CLIENT", "req_id": "REQ-1-1-1", "type": "API", "name": "authApi", "file_path": "frontend/src/features/auth/authApi.ts", "first_line": "1", "responsibility": "HTTP boundary for registration and the shared session path; maps server field-error payloads into typed form errors on top of the shared axios client.", "specification": "Exports registerAccount(payload: RegisterAccountPayload): Promise<RegisteredAccount> (POST /api/auth/register), signInWithPassword(identifier, password): Promise<SessionUser> (POST /api/auth/login), fetchSession(): Promise<SessionUser | null> (GET /api/auth/session), signOut(): Promise<void> (POST /api/auth/logout), and the AuthRequestError class carrying { status, fieldErrors: RegistrationFieldErrors }. All calls go through frontend/src/api/index.ts (axios instance baseURL '/api') which owns the global error interceptor, so server 400 responses surface complete multi-field error maps. Must not fabricate local fallbacks when the request fails.", "inputs": "{ username, email, password, confirmPassword, agreeToTerms } for registration; identifier/password for sign-in; no input for session lookup/logout.", "outputs": "RegisteredAccount { id, username, email, emailVerified: true }; SessionUser { id, username, email }; null when signed out; AuthRequestError with fieldErrors on validation failure.", "callers": [], "callees": [], "test_focus": "400 responses populate all failing field messages at once; AuthRequestError exposes status and per-field text so the page can render itemized messages; session lookup returns null when unauthenticated."}

API-REQ-1-1-1-AUTH-ROUTES.content: {"interface_id": "API-REQ-1-1-1-AUTH-ROUTES", "req_id": "REQ-1-1-1", "type": "API", "name": "authRoutes", "file_path": "backend/src/routes/authRoutes.js", "first_line": "1", "responsibility": "Express router owning POST /api/auth/register, POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/session, POST /api/auth/logout and the HTTP status/shape contract for each.", "specification": "CommonJS module exporting an express.Router, mounted at /api/auth in backend/src/app.js (the app.js import exists; the one-line `app.use('/api/auth', authRoutes);` mount is deferred to the TDD stage because the DESIGN write budget was reached). Register: 201 { code, message, data: { id, username, email, emailVerified: true } } and starts the session so sign-in is immediately available; 400 { code, message, errors: { username?, email?, password?, confirmPassword?, terms? } } returning all failing fields together. Login: 200 { data: SessionUser } / 401 with an error entry. Session: 200 { data: SessionUser | null }. Logout: 200 and clears the cookie. Route handlers stay thin and delegate to authService; no validation or SQL logic in the router.", "inputs": "JSON bodies { username, email, password, confirmPassword, agreeToTerms } and { identifier, password }; session cookie on session/logout requests.", "outputs": "JSON envelopes { code, message, data } or { code, message, errors } plus the session cookie.", "callers": [], "callees": [], "test_focus": "Supertest route tests: 201 creates a sign-in-capable verified account; 400 lists username+email+password+confirmPassword+terms errors in a single response; duplicate username returns 'Username already exists'; invalid email returns 'Email format is invalid' while retaining both attempted values; session endpoint restores the signed-in user."}

DB-REQ-1-1-1-ACCOUNTS-SCHEMA.content: {"interface_id": "DB-REQ-1-1-1-ACCOUNTS-SCHEMA", "req_id": "REQ-1-1-1", "type": "DB", "name": "accounts and sessions schema", "file_path": "backend/src/database/init_db.js", "first_line": "60", "responsibility": "Idempotent schema for sign-in-capable accounts (with verified-email status) and the durable sessions backing global authenticated state.", "specification": "Add CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements to initializeDatabase's schema block (no new one-off connection helpers): accounts(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, username TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL, email_verified INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) and sessions(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, token TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, account_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id), created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP). email_verified is set true on registration because this product marks the email verified directly and exposes no verification page. Schema evolution stays idempotent and centralized in this file.", "inputs": "initializeDatabase() call at backend startup and from tests via the shared harness.", "outputs": "Tables available for authService queries through db_runtime helpers.", "callers": [], "callees": [], "test_focus": "Tables exist after initializeDatabase; username and email uniqueness constraints reject duplicate inserts; sessions rows can be looked up by token; re-running initialization is idempotent."}

DB-REQ-1-1-1-SEED-ACCOUNT.content: {"interface_id": "DB-REQ-1-1-1-SEED-ACCOUNT", "req_id": "REQ-1-1-1", "type": "DB", "name": "seedDatabase default account", "file_path": "backend/src/database/seed_db.js", "first_line": "4", "responsibility": "Deterministic, idempotent seed of the pre-existing account named by the requirement scenarios so a fresh unauthenticated session can sign in with real persisted data.", "specification": "Inside the existing withTransaction block, INSERT OR IGNORE the account alice-dev / alice.dev@example.test with password Valid-password-123! hashed by the same scheme authService verifies against, email_verified = 1, and an explicit stable id so repeated seeding neither duplicates nor mutates the record. The comment in the file already records the exact required statements; the TDD stage implements them. Reached through the normal seed entrypoint (npm seed / seedDatabase()) that tests can reuse; no frontend constants, fallback arrays, or test-only endpoints.", "inputs": "seedDatabase() invocation from the application bootstrap path or the shared test harness.", "outputs": "One persisted, sign-in-capable account row with verified email.", "callers": [], "callees": [], "test_focus": "After seeding, alice-dev / Valid-password-123! authenticates through POST /api/auth/login; running the seed twice leaves exactly one row; registration of a different username still succeeds alongside the seeded account."}

FUNC-REQ-1-1-1-AUTH-SERVICE.content: {"interface_id": "FUNC-REQ-1-1-1-AUTH-SERVICE", "req_id": "REQ-1-1-1", "type": "FUNC", "name": "authService", "file_path": "backend/src/services/authService.js", "first_line": "1", "responsibility": "Registration, credential verification, and durable session logic: aggregates all field validation errors, enforces username/email uniqueness, persists a sign-in-capable account marked email-verified, and owns session creation/lookup/destruction.", "specification": "Exports SESSION_COOKIE_NAME ('arc_session'), registerAccount(input) -> { ok: true, account } | { ok: false, errors } (errors includes every failing field and never reveals a password), authenticate(identifier, password) -> { ok: true, user } | { ok: false, errors }, getSessionUser(sessionToken) -> user | null, createSession(userId) -> token, destroySession(sessionToken). Returned user objects expose only { id, username, email }. All SQL goes through backend/src/database/db_runtime.js helpers; passwords are hashed and never returned to callers. Validation is delegated to authValidation; uniqueness conflicts are checked against the accounts table.", "inputs": "Registration input object; identifier+password credentials; session token strings; userId.", "outputs": "{ ok, account|user } success envelopes or { ok: false, errors } field-error maps; opaque session tokens.", "callers": [], "callees": [], "test_focus": "Multiple invalid fields return one aggregated error map; no row is inserted when validation fails; successful registration creates a row with email_verified = 1 and a verifiable password hash; duplicate username/email is rejected; session token round-trips through getSessionUser so the signed-in state survives reload."}

FUNC-REQ-1-1-1-AUTH-VALIDATION.content: {"interface_id": "FUNC-REQ-1-1-1-AUTH-VALIDATION", "req_id": "REQ-1-1-1", "type": "FUNC", "name": "authValidation", "file_path": "backend/src/services/validation/authValidation.js", "first_line": "1", "responsibility": "Pure validation rules and canonical field-message constants for registration input, evaluated together so every failing field is reported in one pass.", "specification": "CommonJS module exporting USERNAME_PATTERN, USERNAME_MAX_LENGTH (39), EMAIL_MAX_LENGTH (254), PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH (12), PASSWORD_MAX_LENGTH (128), FIELD_MESSAGES, isValidUsername, validateEmail, isValidPassword, passwordsMatch, validateRegistrationInput. Rules: username is 1-39 lowercase ASCII letters/digits with single internal hyphens and no leading/trailing hyphen; email is trimmed then must be <= 254 chars with exactly one '@', at least one dot after '@' and non-empty domain labels; password is 12-128 chars with at least one uppercase, one lowercase, one digit, one non-alphanumeric special character and no whitespace; confirmation must equal the password; terms must be checked. validateRegistrationInput returns { errors, normalized: { username, email } } including every violated rule; messages match FIELD_MESSAGES exactly ('Username format is invalid', 'Username already exists', 'Email format is invalid', 'Password requirements are not satisfied', 'Agree to terms is required'). isValidUsername/isValidPassword are implemented; validateEmail, passwordsMatch, and validateRegistrationInput are declared contracts left to the TDD stage.", "inputs": "Raw field values (unknown types tolerated) for username, email, password, confirmPassword, agreeToTerms.", "outputs": "Booleans from the predicates; { errors: Record<string, string>, normalized: { username, email } } from validateRegistrationInput.", "callers": [], "callees": [], "test_focus": "Unit tests for boundary usernames (39 chars ok, 40 rejected, leading/trailing hyphen rejected, uppercase rejected), emails (exactly one '@', 254-char limit, missing dot, empty domain label, surrounding whitespace trimmed), passwords (each required character class, whitespace rejected, 12/128 boundaries), confirmation mismatch, and a combined case asserting all messages are returned together."}

Keeps public routes reachable while unauthenticated; the home page's 'Sign in' control navigates to /login and the sign-in page's unique 'Create an account' link navigates to /signup. Route registration stays thin — no feature logic in App.tsx.", "inputs": "Browser navigation; session status from AuthSessionContext.", "outputs": "Rendered page for '/', '/login', '/signup' with shared session context; SPA fallback served by the backend on port 3411.", "callers": [], "callees": [], "test_focus": "Route tests render the registration page at /signup and the sign-in page at /login; navigating from home 'Sign in' to the sign-in page and then to 'Create an account' reaches the registration form; the backend-hosted build serves these routes on port 3411."}

UI-REQ-1-1-1-REGISTER-PAGE.content: {"interface_id": "UI-REQ-1-1-1-REGISTER-PAGE", "req_id": "REQ-1-1-1", "type": "UI", "name": "RegisterPage", "file_path": "frontend/src/pages/RegisterPage.tsx", "first_line": "1", "responsibility": "Owns the registration form surface at /signup: exactly one Username textbox, one Email textbox, one Password input, one Confirm password input, one initially unchecked 'Agree to the terms' checkbox, and one enabled 'Create account' button, with one message slot per field.", "specification": "React TSX default-exported component. Accessible labels must match: 'Username', 'Email', 'Password', 'Confirm password', 'Agree to the terms', 'Create account'. Password inputs are type=password and their values must never be rendered as text in the page body. On success the node adopts the session (AuthSessionContext) and redirects to the sign-in page. On failure it stays mounted, keeps the attempted username and email state (values are only cleared on success), renders every returned field message next to its field ('Username already exists' | 'Username format is invalid', 'Email format is invalid', 'Password requirements are not satisfied', 'Agree to terms is required') and leaves the submit button enabled. Contains the link to the sign-in page for returning users.", "inputs": "User keystrokes on username/email/password/confirmPassword and the terms checkbox; registration response from authApi.registerAccount (RegisteredAccount or AuthRequestError with fieldErrors).", "outputs": "Rendered labeled form with per-field error text; calls into authApi.registerAccount; updates global session via AuthSessionContext; navigates to /login on success.", "callers": [], "callees": [], "test_focus": "Registration page renders all six controls with exact labels and an enabled submit button; every failing field message appears together in one submission (leading-hyphen username, 'not-an-email', 'short' password, mismatched confirmation, unchecked terms); attempted username/email retained after failure and no account created; password never echoed; successful registration reaches the sign-in page."}

UI-REQ-1-1-1-SESSION-CONTEXT.content: {"interface_id": "UI-REQ-1-1-1-SESSION-CONTEXT", "req_id": "REQ-1-1-1", "type": "UI", "name": "AuthSessionProvider / useAuthSession", "file_path": "frontend/src/features/auth/AuthSessionContext.tsx", "first_line": "1", "responsibility": "Single global source of truth for the authenticated user (user, status, setUser, refreshSession) consumed by every page and shell so registration/sign-in transitions and reload recovery are consistent.", "specification": "React context provider exposing AuthSessionValue { user: SessionUser | null; status: 'loading' | 'authenticated' | 'unauthenticated'; refreshSession(): Promise<void>; setUser(user | null): void }.
